q: 你今天头疼___？
zh: 你今天头疼吗？
py: nǐ jīn tiān tóu téng ma
why: A plain statement becomes a neutral yes/no question with 吗. 呢 only follows a noun or an existing question, and 嘛 states the obvious instead of asking.
en: Do you have a headache today?

q: 你哪儿不舒服___？
zh: 你哪儿不舒服？
py: nǐ nǎ r bù shū fu
why: 哪儿 already makes this a question asking for information, so no 吗 or 吧 may be added. The blank stays empty.
en: Where do you feel unwell?

q: 你昨天晚上睡得好不好___？
zh: 你昨天晚上睡得好不好？
py: nǐ zuó tiān wǎn shang shuì de hǎo bù hǎo
why: 睡得好不好 is an A-not-A question, which is already complete. Adding 吗 doubles the question, and 吧 would turn it into a guess.
en: Did you sleep well last night?

q: 我刚搬来这儿，不知道这里的冬天比北京冷___？
zh: 我刚搬来这儿，不知道这里的冬天比北京冷吗？
py: wǒ gāng bān lái zhè r bù zhī dào zhè lǐ de dōng tiān bǐ běi jīng lěng ma
why: The speaker has no opinion and wants a plain yes or no, so the statement takes 吗. 嘛 would claim the answer is obvious, which the first clause denies.
en: I just moved here and do not know: is the winter here colder than in Beijing?

q: 医生，我这个病需要住院___？
zh: 医生，我这个病需要住院吗？
py: yī shēng wǒ zhè ge bìng xū yào zhù yuàn ma
why: A yes/no question about a statement needs 吗. 呢 cannot turn a statement into a question, and 嘛 would insist the answer is obvious.
en: Doctor, do I need to be admitted to hospital?

q: 你是想知道明天会不会下雪___？
zh: 你是想知道明天会不会下雪吗？
py: nǐ shì xiǎng zhī dào míng tiān huì bù huì xià xuě ma
why: 会不会下雪 is only embedded inside 想知道; the whole sentence is a statement about the listener, so asking it needs 吗. Leaving it empty gives a plain statement.
en: Do you want to know whether it will snow tomorrow?

q: 你知道医院附近哪儿有药店___？
zh: 你知道医院附近哪儿有药店吗？
py: nǐ zhī dào yī yuàn fù jìn nǎ r yǒu yào diàn ma
why: Here 哪儿 sits inside 知道, so the sentence asks only yes or no and takes 吗. Without it this would be a statement; 呢 cannot make a yes/no question.
en: Do you know where there is a pharmacy near the hospital?

q: 你感冒___吗？
zh: 你感冒了吗？
py: nǐ gǎn mào le ma
why: Asking whether something has happened keeps the 了 inside the statement and adds 吗 at the end. The other particles cannot sit before 吗 here.
en: Have you caught a cold?

q: 我有点儿头疼，你___？
zh: 我有点儿头疼，你呢？
py: wǒ yǒu diǎn r tóu téng nǐ ne
why: Bouncing the question back with a bare pronoun is 你呢. 你吗 is not said because 吗 needs a full statement before it.
en: I have a bit of a headache. What about you?

q: 我的雨伞___？
zh: 我的雨伞呢？
py: wǒ de yǔ sǎn ne
why: A noun alone plus 呢 asks where it is. 吗 would need a complete statement.
en: Where is my umbrella?

q: 今天下雨，明天___？
zh: 今天下雨，明天呢？
py: jīn tiān xià yǔ míng tiān ne
why: Following up with a bare noun asks the same question about tomorrow, which is 明天呢. 吧 would be a guess about tomorrow.
en: It is raining today. What about tomorrow?

q: 春天很短，你们那儿的秋天___？
zh: 春天很短，你们那儿的秋天呢？
py: chūn tiān hěn duǎn nǐ men nà r de qiū tiān ne
why: A topic phrase with no verb that asks about another item in the same frame takes 呢. 吗 would need a full clause like 秋天也很短吗.
en: Spring is short. What about autumn where you are?

q: 这么冷的天，你怎么还穿短袖___？
zh: 这么冷的天，你怎么还穿短袖呢？
py: zhè me lěng de tiān nǐ zěn me hái chuān duǎn xiù ne
why: 怎么 makes this a question already, so 吗 and 吧 are impossible. 呢 only softens it and adds the speaker's puzzlement.
en: It is so cold. Why are you still in short sleeves?

q: 医生让你每天吃几次药___？
zh: 医生让你每天吃几次药呢？
py: yī shēng ràng nǐ měi tiān chī jǐ cì yào ne
why: 几次 is a question word, so 吗 cannot follow. 吧 would turn it into a guess. Only 呢 can soften an existing question.
en: How many times a day did the doctor tell you to take the medicine?

q: 要是明天还下雨，我们的运动会该怎么办___？
zh: 要是明天还下雨，我们的运动会该怎么办呢？
py: yào shi míng tiān hái xià yǔ wǒ men de yùn dòng huì gāi zěn me bàn ne
why: The question word 怎么办 already asks, so 吗 is out and 吧 would turn it into a suggestion. 呢 gives the worried tone of a thinking-aloud question.
en: If it still rains tomorrow, what are we going to do about the sports day?

q: 你到底是头疼还是肚子疼___？
zh: 你到底是头疼还是肚子疼呢？
py: nǐ dào dǐ shì tóu téng hái shi dù zi téng ne
why: 还是 offers a choice, so the sentence is already a question and 吗 is ungrammatical. 呢 adds the impatient tone of 到底.
en: Is it your head or your stomach that hurts, exactly?

q: 别进去，医生在看病___。
zh: 别进去，医生在看病呢。
py: bié jìn qù yī shēng zài kàn bìng ne
why: 在 + verb shows an action in progress, and 呢 points out that this is the situation right now. 吗 would ask a question and 吧 would turn it into a guess.
en: Do not go in; the doctor is seeing a patient.

q: 我还没吃药___。
zh: 我还没吃药呢。
py: wǒ hái méi chī yào ne
why: 还没 means nothing has happened yet, so 了 is impossible. 呢 marks that this is still the situation.
en: I have not taken my medicine yet.

q: 外面刮着大风___。
zh: 外面刮着大风呢。
py: wài miàn guā zhe dà fēng ne
why: 着 shows a continuing state and 呢 stresses that it is going on now. 的 would be an assurance and 吗 a question.
en: It is blowing a gale outside.

q: 现在才十月___，怎么就穿羽绒服了？
zh: 现在才十月呢，怎么就穿羽绒服了？
py: xiàn zài cái shí yuè ne zěn me jiù chuān yǔ róng fú le
why: 才 + time + 呢 stresses that it is early, against the listener's assumption. 了 cannot follow 才十月, and 吗 and 吧 do not fit.
en: It is only October. Why are you in a down jacket already?

q: 他还没退烧___，不能去上学。
zh: 他还没退烧呢，不能去上学。
py: tā hái méi tuì shāo ne bù néng qù shàng xué
why: 还没 + verb + 呢 says the situation has not changed. 了 contradicts 还没, and 吧 would turn a fact into a guess.
en: His fever has not come down yet, so he cannot go to school.

q: 我正在量体温___，你等一下。
zh: 我正在量体温呢，你等一下。
py: wǒ zhèng zài liáng tǐ wēn ne nǐ děng yī xià
why: 正在 marks an action in progress and 呢 closes it as how things stand now. 吧 would suggest something rather than describe it.
en: I am taking my temperature right now; wait a moment.

q: 山上还下着雪___，路不好走。
zh: 山上还下着雪呢，路不好走。
py: shān shàng hái xià zhe xuě ne lù bù hǎo zǒu
why: 着 and 还 show the snow continues, and 呢 stresses that it is still so. 了 would announce a new change, and 吗 asks.
en: It is still snowing up in the mountains, so the road is hard to walk.

q: 这点儿雨算什么？我才不怕___！
zh: 这点儿雨算什么？我才不怕呢！
py: zhè diǎn r yǔ suàn shén me wǒ cái bù pà ne
why: 才不...呢 is the strong denial: "I certainly do not". 了 would mean the fear has just stopped, which is not the idea here.
en: What is a bit of rain? I am certainly not afraid!

q: 现在是三伏天，最热的时候还没到___，你就受不了了？
zh: 现在是三伏天，最热的时候还没到呢，你就受不了了？
py: xiàn zài shì sān fú tiān zuì rè de shí hou hái méi dào ne nǐ jiù shòu bù liǎo le
why: 还没到 means not yet, so the clause takes 呢 and never 了. 吗 would turn the clause into a question in the middle of a sentence.
en: It is the dog days, but the hottest time has not even come yet, and you cannot stand it already?

q: 医生说他的病还没好___，你怎么能让他出门吹风？
zh: 医生说他的病还没好呢，你怎么能让他出门吹风？
py: yī shēng shuō tā de bìng hái méi hǎo ne nǐ zěn me néng ràng tā chū mén chuī fēng
why: 还没好 describes a state that has not changed, which is 呢. 了 would say he has recovered, and the following reproach would make no sense.
en: The doctor said he is not better yet, so how can you let him go out in the wind?

q: 天冷了，你多穿一件衣服___。
zh: 天冷了，你多穿一件衣服吧。
py: tiān lěng le nǐ duō chuān yī jiàn yī fu ba
why: A friendly instruction softened into advice takes 吧. 吗 would ask whether you put one on.
en: It is cold; put on another layer.

q: 我们去公园走走___。
zh: 我们去公园走走吧。
py: wǒ men qù gōng yuán zǒu zou ba
why: "Let us" is a proposal, so 吧 is needed. 我们去公园走走吗 would ask if the plan exists, not propose it.
en: Let us take a walk in the park.

q: 你感冒了，今天请假在家休息___。
zh: 你感冒了，今天请假在家休息吧。
py: nǐ gǎn mào le jīn tiān qǐng jià zài jiā xiū xi ba
why: Advice to do something is 吧. 吗 would ask whether you are taking leave, and 呢 describes a state instead of advising.
en: You have a cold; take the day off and rest at home.

q: 雨太大了，我们等雨停了再走___。
zh: 雨太大了，我们等雨停了再走吧。
py: yǔ tài dà le wǒ men děng yǔ tíng le zài zǒu ba
why: "Let us wait and then go" is a proposal, which 吧 marks. 吗 would ask a factual question about the plan.
en: The rain is too heavy; let us wait until it stops before leaving.

q: 我真不想去医院，不过你说得对。好___，我明天就去。
zh: 我真不想去医院，不过你说得对。好吧，我明天就去。
py: wǒ zhēn bù xiǎng qù yī yuàn bú guò nǐ shuō de duì hǎo ba wǒ míng tiān jiù qù
why: 好吧 means giving in reluctantly after resistance. 好啊 would sound eager and does not match 我真不想去.
en: I really do not want to go to the hospital, but you are right. All right then, I will go tomorrow.

q: 这个药很苦，你捏着鼻子一口喝下去___。
zh: 这个药很苦，你捏着鼻子一口喝下去吧。
py: zhè ge yào hěn kǔ nǐ niē zhe bí zi yī kǒu hē xià qù ba
why: A gentle instruction is softened with 吧. 吗 would ask a question and 的 gives an assurance about the future, neither of which fits an order.
en: This medicine is bitter; hold your nose and drink it down in one go.

q: 明天的天气预报说有大雨，我们把爬山的计划改到下个周末___。
zh: 明天的天气预报说有大雨，我们把爬山的计划改到下个周末吧。
py: míng tiān de tiān qì yù bào shuō yǒu dà yǔ wǒ men bǎ pá shān de jì huà gǎi dào xià ge zhōu mò ba
why: Proposing a change to the plan is 吧. 了 would report that the change has already been made, which a proposal does not do.
en: The forecast says heavy rain tomorrow; let us move the hiking plan to next weekend.

q: 你已经咳嗽一个星期了，别再拖了，今天下午就去看医生___。
zh: 你已经咳嗽一个星期了，别再拖了，今天下午就去看医生吧。
py: nǐ yǐ jīng ké sou yī gè xīng qī le bié zài tuō le jīn tiān xià wǔ jiù qù kàn yī shēng ba
why: After "stop putting it off" the sentence urges an action, so it ends in 吧. 吗 would ask whether you are going.
en: You have been coughing for a week; stop putting it off and go and see a doctor this afternoon.

q: 你的脸很红，你发烧了___？
zh: 你的脸很红，你发烧了吧？
py: nǐ de liǎn hěn hóng nǐ fā shāo le ba
why: The red face gives the speaker a guess and the 吧 seeks confirmation. Neutral 吗 would ignore the evidence the speaker already has.
en: Your face is very red; you have a fever, haven't you?

q: 今天好冷，你也觉得冷___？
zh: 今天好冷，你也觉得冷吧？
py: jīn tiān hǎo lěng nǐ yě jué de lěng ba
why: The speaker feels cold and expects agreement, which is 吧. 嘛 would say it is obvious rather than seek agreement.
en: It is so cold today; you think so too, right?

q: 他大概感冒了___，一直在咳嗽。
zh: 他大概感冒了吧，一直在咳嗽。
py: tā dà gài gǎn mào le ba yī zhí zài ké sou
why: 大概 shows a guess, and 吧 marks the guess. 吗 asks a neutral question and cannot go with 大概 in a statement.
en: He has probably caught a cold, I suppose; he keeps coughing.

q: 这个周末应该不会下雨了___？
zh: 这个周末应该不会下雨了吧？
py: zhè ge zhōu mò yīng gāi bú huì xià yǔ le ba
why: 应该 shows the speaker expects a certain answer, which is what 吧 seeks to confirm. 吗 would be a neutral question without that expectation.
en: It should not rain this weekend, should it?

q: 你每天都跑步，身体一定很好___？
zh: 你每天都跑步，身体一定很好吧？
py: nǐ měi tiān dōu pǎo bù shēn tǐ yī dìng hěn hǎo ba
why: 一定 shows the speaker is already sure and only wants agreement, so 吧. 吗 would show no opinion at all.
en: You run every day, so you must be very healthy, I suppose?

q: 你的腿疼了好几天了，你一定没有好好休息___？
zh: 你的腿疼了好几天了，你一定没有好好休息吧？
py: nǐ de tuǐ téng le hǎo jǐ tiān le nǐ yī dìng méi yǒu hǎo hǎo xiū xi ba
why: 一定 plus the visible evidence makes this a presumption, so 吧. 吗 would suggest the speaker has no idea either way.
en: Your leg has hurt for days; you surely have not been resting properly, have you?

q: 我看你脸色不太好，昨天晚上大概没睡好___？
zh: 我看你脸色不太好，昨天晚上大概没睡好吧？
py: wǒ kàn nǐ liǎn sè bú tài hǎo zuó tiān wǎn shang dà gài méi shuì hǎo ba
why: 大概 and the speaker's observation mark this as a guess to be confirmed: 吧. 了 cannot follow 没睡好 when the point is a guess.
en: You do not look well; you probably did not sleep well last night, I take it?

q: 今年夏天比去年热得多，空调的电费应该不便宜___？
zh: 今年夏天比去年热得多，空调的电费应该不便宜吧？
py: jīn nián xià tiān bǐ qù nián rè de duō kōng tiáo de diàn fèi yīng gāi bù pián yi ba
why: 应该 plus the reasoning from the hot weather is a presumption to confirm, so 吧. 吗 would ignore that reasoning.
en: This summer is much hotter than last year; the air-conditioning bill must be steep, I suppose?

q: 今天的天气多好___！
zh: 今天的天气多好啊！
py: jīn tiān de tiān qì duō hǎo a
why: 多 + adjective makes an exclamation and 啊 adds the warmth. 吗 would turn it into a question and 吧 into a guess.
en: What lovely weather today!

q: 雪下得真大___！
zh: 雪下得真大啊！
py: xuě xià de zhēn dà a
why: 真 + adjective is an exclamation, and 啊 gives it feeling. 吗 and 吧 would change the sentence type.
en: It is snowing so hard!

q: 快穿上外套___，外面很冷！
zh: 快穿上外套啊，外面很冷！
py: kuài chuān shàng wài tào a wài miàn hěn lěng
why: A friendly urging is warmed by 啊. 吗 would ask a question and 呢 describes ongoing action rather than urges.
en: Hurry and put on your coat; it is cold outside!

q: 今年的秋天真舒服。——是___，比往年凉快多了。
zh: 今年的秋天真舒服。——是啊，比往年凉快多了。
py: jīn nián de qiū tiān zhēn shū fu shì a bǐ wǎng nián liáng kuai duō le
why: 是啊 is warm agreement. 是吗 would mean "is that so?", the speaker does not know, which contradicts the reply that follows.
en: "This autumn is really pleasant." "Yes, it is much cooler than in previous years."

q: 您多保重身体___，别太累了！
zh: 您多保重身体啊，别太累了！
py: nín duō bǎo zhòng shēn tǐ a bié tài lèi le
why: A caring farewell with a request is warmed by 啊. 吗 would ask a question and 呢 would describe a continuing state.
en: Take good care of yourself and do not get too tired!

q: 你看，雨后的空气多新鲜___，咱们出去走走吧！
zh: 你看，雨后的空气多新鲜啊，咱们出去走走吧！
py: nǐ kàn yǔ hòu de kōng qì duō xīn xiān a zán men chū qù zǒu zou ba
why: 多 + adjective is an exclamation, so the clause ends in 啊. 吗 would ask whether it is fresh and 吧 would make a guess.
en: Look, how fresh the air is after the rain! Let us go out for a walk.

q: 能在这么热的天气里喝上一杯冰水，真是舒服___！
zh: 能在这么热的天气里喝上一杯冰水，真是舒服啊！
py: néng zài zhè me rè de tiān qì lǐ hē shàng yī bēi bīng shuǐ zhēn shi shū fu a
why: 真是 + adjective is a heartfelt exclamation, which 啊 colours. 吗 and 吧 would turn it into a question or a guess.
en: What a pleasure to have a glass of iced water in such hot weather!

q: 生病了当然要吃药___。
zh: 生病了当然要吃药嘛。
py: shēng bìng le dāng rán yào chī yào ma
why: 当然 says this is obvious, and 嘛 carries "as everyone knows". 吗 would ask a question, which clashes with 当然.
en: Of course you have to take medicine when you are ill.

q: 冷就多穿点___。
zh: 冷就多穿点呗。
py: lěng jiù duō chuān diǎn bei
why: 就...呗 says the fix is simple, so just do it. 吗 would ask whether you wear more.
en: If you are cold, just put on more.

q: 他才五岁___，生病了当然会哭。
zh: 他才五岁嘛，生病了当然会哭。
py: tā cái wǔ suì ma shēng bìng le dāng rán huì kū
why: 嘛 points to an obvious reason ("he is only five, after all"). 吗 would ask how old he is, and the clause is meant as a reason.
en: He is only five, after all; of course he cries when he is ill.

q: 下雨就下雨___，我们有雨伞，怕什么。
zh: 下雨就下雨呗，我们有雨伞，怕什么。
py: xià yǔ jiù xià yǔ bei wǒ men yǒu yǔ sǎn pà shén me
why: X 就 X 呗 means "so be it" with a shrug. 吗 would make it a question and does not fit the follow-up 怕什么.
en: If it rains, then it rains. We have umbrellas, so what is there to fear?

q: 医生早就说过了___，抽烟对身体不好。
zh: 医生早就说过了嘛，抽烟对身体不好。
py: yī shēng zǎo jiù shuō guo le ma chōu yān duì shēn tǐ bù hǎo
why: 嘛 reminds the listener of something they should already know. 吗 would ask whether the doctor said it, which the clause after contradicts.
en: The doctor said so long ago, you know: smoking is bad for your health.

q: 睡不着就别睡___，起来看会儿书，反正明天不用上班。
zh: 睡不着就别睡呗，起来看会儿书，反正明天不用上班。
py: shuì bù zháo jiù bié shuì bei qǐ lái kàn huì r shū fǎn zhèng míng tiān bú yòng shàng bān
why: 就...呗 with 反正 gives the "no big deal, just do it" attitude. 吗 would turn the clause into a question.
en: If you cannot sleep, then do not sleep; get up and read a while, since you do not have to work tomorrow.

q: 夏天本来就热___，你别老抱怨天气，开着空调就是了。
zh: 夏天本来就热嘛，你别老抱怨天气，开着空调就是了。
py: xià tiān běn lái jiù rè ma nǐ bié lǎo bào yuàn tiān qì kāi zhe kōng tiáo jiù shì le
why: 本来就 states the obvious, so 嘛 fits. 吗 would ask whether summer is hot, and the clause then makes no sense.
en: Summer is hot by nature, after all; stop always complaining about the weather and just keep the air conditioning on.

q: 你自己都说不舒服了，那就去医院看看___，别在这儿犹豫了。
zh: 你自己都说不舒服了，那就去医院看看呗，别在这儿犹豫了。
py: nǐ zì jǐ dōu shuō bù shū fu le nà jiù qù yī yuàn kàn kan bei bié zài zhè r yóu yù le
why: 那就...呗 treats going as the obvious simple answer. 吗 would ask whether you will go, which clashes with the order that follows.
en: You said yourself you feel unwell, so just go and have it checked at the hospital; stop hesitating.

q: 别担心，你的病会好___。
zh: 别担心，你的病会好的。
py: bié dān xīn nǐ de bìng huì hǎo de
why: 会 + verb + 的 gives a calm assurance about the future. 了 reports a change that has already happened.
en: Do not worry, you will get better.

q: 你放心，明天一定会放晴___。
zh: 你放心，明天一定会放晴的。
py: nǐ fàng xīn míng tiān yī dìng huì fàng qíng de
why: 一定会...的 is a confident promise. 吧 would make it a mere guess and 了 would claim it has already happened.
en: Rest assured, it will definitely clear up tomorrow.

q: 吃了药，烧很快就会退___。
zh: 吃了药，烧很快就会退的。
py: chī le yào shāo hěn kuài jiù huì tuì de
why: 会...的 reassures about a future result. 了 reports a change already done, which clashes with 会.
en: Once you take the medicine, the fever will soon go down.

q: 我不会忘记吃药___，你不用提醒我。
zh: 我不会忘记吃药的，你不用提醒我。
py: wǒ bú huì wàng jì chī yào de nǐ bú yòng tí xǐng wǒ
why: 不会...的 is a promise that something will not happen. 吧 would turn the promise into a guess.
en: I will not forget to take my medicine; you do not need to remind me.

q: 台风很快就会过去___，大家不要太紧张。
zh: 台风很快就会过去的，大家不要太紧张。
py: tái fēng hěn kuài jiù huì guò qù de dà jiā bú yào tài jǐn zhāng
why: The speaker reassures the group about the future with 会...的. 了 would say it has already passed, which contradicts 不要太紧张 still being needed.
en: The typhoon will pass soon, so everyone, do not be too nervous.

q: 医生说手术很安全，你妈妈一定不会有事___，别一个人在这儿哭了。
zh: 医生说手术很安全，你妈妈一定不会有事的，别一个人在这儿哭了。
py: yī shēng shuō shǒu shù hěn ān quán nǐ mā ma yī dìng bú huì yǒu shì de bié yī gè rén zài zhè r kū le
why: 一定不会...的 comforts the listener with certainty. 吧 would make the comfort a weak guess and defeat the reassurance.
en: The doctor said the operation is very safe, so your mother will surely be fine; stop crying here alone.

q: 我的头不疼___。
zh: 我的头不疼了。
py: wǒ de tóu bù téng le
why: 不 + verb + 了 means "not any more", a change from before. 呢 would say it still hurts.
en: My head does not hurt any more.

q: 天晴___，我们出去玩吧。
zh: 天晴了，我们出去玩吧。
py: tiān qíng le wǒ men chū qù wán ba
why: The weather has changed from before, which 了 marks. 呢 would say it is still sunny as before.
en: The sky has cleared; let us go out to play.

q: 她已经不咳嗽___，明天可以上学。
zh: 她已经不咳嗽了，明天可以上学。
py: tā yǐ jīng bù ké sou le míng tiān kě yǐ shàng xué
why: 已经不 + verb needs 了 for "not any more". 的 would be a promise about the future, which is not the point.
en: She does not cough any more, so she can go to school tomorrow.

q: 秋天到了，树叶都黄___。
zh: 秋天到了，树叶都黄了。
py: qiū tiān dào le shù yè dōu huáng le
why: 都黄了 says the leaves have changed colour, which is a new state. 呢 would say they are yellow as things stand, without the change.
en: Autumn has come; the leaves have all turned yellow.

q: 我现在每天跑步，身体比以前好多___。
zh: 我现在每天跑步，身体比以前好多了。
py: wǒ xiàn zài měi tiān pǎo bù shēn tǐ bǐ yǐ qián hǎo duō le
why: 比以前好多了 compares the present with the past, a change, so 了 is needed. 吗 would ask and 的 would assure.
en: I run every day now, and I am much healthier than before.

q: 孩子的烧退了以后，就不再哭闹___，也肯吃东西了。
zh: 孩子的烧退了以后，就不再哭闹了，也肯吃东西了。
py: hái zi de shāo tuì le yǐ hòu jiù bú zài kū nào le yě kěn chī dōng xi le
why: 不再 + verb + 了 marks "no longer" after a change. 呢 would say he is still fussing, which clashes with 烧退了.
en: After the child's fever went down, he stopped crying and fussing and was willing to eat again.

q: 他以前很怕打针，现在长大了，一点儿也不怕___。
zh: 他以前很怕打针，现在长大了，一点儿也不怕了。
py: tā yǐ qián hěn pà dǎ zhēn xiàn zài zhǎng dà le yī diǎn r yě bú pà le
why: 以前...现在 sets up a change, so 不怕了 means "not any more". 呢 would stress that he is not afraid at the moment, with no sense of change.
en: He used to be very afraid of injections, but now he has grown up and is not afraid at all any more.

zh: 外面还下着雨呢。
py: wài miàn hái xià zhe yǔ ne
why: 着 and 还 show the rain is continuing, and 呢 closes the sentence. A final particle is always last.
en: It is still raining outside.

zh: 你最近睡得好吗。
py: nǐ zuì jìn shuì de hǎo ma
why: 吗 must come last to turn the statement into a yes/no question. 最近 can sit before or after 你.
en: Have you been sleeping well lately?

zh: 你先去医院检查一下吧。
py: nǐ xiān qù yī yuàn jiǎn chá yī xià ba
why: 先 goes before the verb phrase, and 吧 comes last to soften the advice.
en: Why don't you go to the hospital for a check-up first.

zh: 春天很暖和夏天呢。
py: chūn tiān hěn nuǎn huo xià tiān ne
why: 夏天呢 is a noun plus 呢, asking the same question about another item. 呢 follows the noun directly.
en: Spring is warm. What about summer?

zh: 你昨天大概没睡好吧。
py: nǐ zuó tiān dà gài méi shuì hǎo ba
why: 吧 ends the sentence to seek confirmation of a guess. 大概 may stand before the subject or before the verb phrase.
en: You probably did not sleep well last night, I suppose.

task: Say you do not do it any more.
zh: 我不吃辣的了。
py: wǒ bù chī là de le
why: "Not any more" is 不 + verb + 了. Leaving out 了 would only say you do not eat it, with no change.
en: I do not eat spicy food any more.

src_py: nǐ jīn tiān qù yī yuàn
task: Turn it into a yes/no question.
zh: 你今天去医院吗。
py: nǐ jīn tiān qù yī yuàn ma
why: 吗 at the end turns a statement into a yes/no question. 今天 can come before or after the subject.
en: Are you going to the hospital today?

task: Say it is snowing right now, with 着 and 呢.
zh: 外面下着雪呢。
py: wài miàn xià zhe xuě ne
why: 着 gives the continuing state and 呢 stresses that it is going on now.
en: It is snowing outside.

task: Soften it into a gentle suggestion.
zh: 你多喝水吧。
py: nǐ duō hē shuǐ ba
why: Adding 吧 turns a flat command into friendly advice.
en: Drink more water.

src_py: zhè ge zhōu mò bú xià yǔ
task: Reassure someone: it definitely will not rain this weekend.
zh: 这个周末一定不会下雨的。
py: zhè ge zhōu mò yī dìng bú huì xià yǔ de
why: 一定不会...的 is the reassuring promise about the future. Ending in 了 would say something has changed, which is not the point.
en: It definitely will not rain this weekend.

s: 你今天哪儿不舒服吗？
s_py: nǐ jīn tiān nǎ r bù shū fu ma
zh: 你今天哪儿不舒服？
py: nǐ jīn tiān nǎ r bù shū fu
why: 哪儿 already makes this a question, so 吗 cannot be added.
en: Where do you feel unwell today?

s: 你吃药还是打针吗？
s_py: nǐ chī yào hái shi dǎ zhēn ma
zh: 你吃药还是打针？
py: nǐ chī yào hái shi dǎ zhēn
why: 还是 asks for a choice, so the sentence is already a question and 吗 is wrong.
en: Will you take medicine or have an injection?

s: 你想吃点什么清淡的吗？
s_py: nǐ xiǎng chī diǎn shén me qīng dàn de ma
zh: 你想吃点什么清淡的吗？
py: nǐ xiǎng chī diǎn shén me qīng dàn de ma
why: Here 什么 means "something", not an information question, so the sentence is a yes/no question and 吗 is correct.
en: Would you like something light to eat?

s: 我感冒了，你吗？
s_py: wǒ gǎn mào le nǐ ma
zh: 我感冒了，你呢？
py: wǒ gǎn mào le nǐ ne
why: Bouncing the question back with a bare pronoun is 你呢; 吗 needs a full statement.
en: I have a cold. What about you?

s: 你明天有空呢？
s_py: nǐ míng tiān yǒu kòng ne
zh: 你明天有空吗？
py: nǐ míng tiān yǒu kòng ma
why: 呢 cannot turn a statement into a yes/no question; that is the job of 吗.
en: Are you free tomorrow?

s: 这么大的雪，我们怎么回家呢？
s_py: zhè me dà de xuě wǒ men zěn me huí jiā ne
zh: 这么大的雪，我们怎么回家呢？
py: zhè me dà de xuě wǒ men zěn me huí jiā ne
why: 怎么 already asks the question, and 呢 may be added to soften it. 吗 would be wrong here, but 呢 is correct.
en: With snow this heavy, how are we going to get home?

s: 我还没吃药了。
s_py: wǒ hái méi chī yào le
zh: 我还没吃药呢。
py: wǒ hái méi chī yào ne
why: 还没 means nothing has happened yet, so it cannot take 了. 呢 marks that it is still the case.
en: I have not taken my medicine yet.

s: 雨还没停了，你再等一会儿。
s_py: yǔ hái méi tíng le nǐ zài děng yī huì r
zh: 雨还没停呢，你再等一会儿。
py: yǔ hái méi tíng ne nǐ zài děng yī huì r
why: 还没 never takes 了; 呢 expresses that the rain is still going on.
en: The rain has not stopped yet; wait a bit longer.

s: 他还没退烧呢，你怎么就让他去上学了？
s_py: tā hái méi tuì shāo ne nǐ zěn me jiù ràng tā qù shàng xué le
zh: 他还没退烧呢，你怎么就让他去上学了？
py: tā hái méi tuì shāo ne nǐ zěn me jiù ràng tā qù shàng xué le
why: The first clause uses 还没...呢, and the second clause ends in 了 because letting him go has already happened. Both particles are correct.
en: His fever has not gone down yet, so how could you let him go to school?

s: 你多喝点水吧吗。
s_py: nǐ duō hē diǎn shuǐ ba ma
zh: 你多喝点水吧。
py: nǐ duō hē diǎn shuǐ ba
why: 吧 and 吗 cannot be stacked. The advice needs only 吧.
en: Drink a bit more water.

s: 好吧，我今天不去上班了，在家休息。
s_py: hǎo ba wǒ jīn tiān bú qù shàng bān le zài jiā xiū xi
zh: 好吧，我今天不去上班了，在家休息。
py: hǎo ba wǒ jīn tiān bú qù shàng bān le zài jiā xiū xi
why: 好吧 gives in, and 不...了 shows a change of plan. Both particles are correct.
en: All right then, I will not go to work today; I will rest at home.

s: 你昨晚没睡好吧吗？
s_py: nǐ zuó wǎn méi shuì hǎo ba ma
zh: 你昨晚没睡好吧？
py: nǐ zuó wǎn méi shuì hǎo ba
why: 吧 and 吗 are never used together. A guess takes 吧 alone.
en: You did not sleep well last night, did you?

s: 他应该已经吃过药了吧？
s_py: tā yīng gāi yǐ jīng chī guo yào le ba
zh: 他应该已经吃过药了吧？
py: tā yīng gāi yǐ jīng chī guo yào le ba
why: 应该 shows the guess, so 吧 is right even after 了. A sentence-final 了 and 吧 can sit together.
en: He should have taken his medicine already, right?

s: 今天的天气真好吗！
s_py: jīn tiān de tiān qì zhēn hǎo ma
zh: 今天的天气真好啊！
py: jīn tiān de tiān qì zhēn hǎo a
why: An exclamation with 真 takes 啊. 吗 would turn it into a question, which clashes with the exclamation mark.
en: The weather is so nice today!

s: 你快去看医生啊，别再拖了！
s_py: nǐ kuài qù kàn yī shēng a bié zài tuō le
zh: 你快去看医生啊，别再拖了！
py: nǐ kuài qù kàn yī shēng a bié zài tuō le
why: 啊 warms a friendly urging and does not change the sentence type. The sentence-final 了 after 别再拖 is also correct.
en: Hurry and see a doctor; stop putting it off!

s: 我早就说你应该去医院吗，你怎么不听呢？
s_py: wǒ zǎo jiù shuō nǐ yīng gāi qù yī yuàn ma nǐ zěn me bù tīng ne
zh: 我早就说你应该去医院嘛，你怎么不听呢？
py: wǒ zǎo jiù shuō nǐ yīng gāi qù yī yuàn ma nǐ zěn me bù tīng ne
why: The speaker is pointing out something obvious, which is 嘛. 吗 would ask a question, which clashes with the reproach.
en: I told you long ago that you should go to the hospital; why will you not listen?

s: 感冒了就多喝水呗。
s_py: gǎn mào le jiù duō hē shuǐ bei
zh: 感冒了就多喝水呗。
py: gǎn mào le jiù duō hē shuǐ bei
why: 就...呗 says the fix is simple. It is informal but fully correct.
en: If you have a cold, just drink more water.

s: 别担心，明天一定会晴了。
s_py: bié dān xīn míng tiān yī dìng huì qíng le
zh: 别担心，明天一定会晴的。
py: bié dān xīn míng tiān yī dìng huì qíng de
why: Reassurance about the future is 会...的. 了 reports a change that has happened, so it cannot follow 一定会.
en: Do not worry, tomorrow will definitely be sunny.

s: 我已经不发烧。
s_py: wǒ yǐ jīng bù fā shāo
zh: 我已经不发烧了。
py: wǒ yǐ jīng bù fā shāo le
why: "Not any more" needs 了 at the end: 不 + verb + 了. Without it the sentence is incomplete.
en: I do not have a fever any more.

s: 她现在是一名护士了，以前在药店工作。
s_py: tā xiàn zài shì yī míng hù shi le yǐ qián zài yào diàn gōng zuò
zh: 她现在是一名护士了，以前在药店工作。
py: tā xiàn zài shì yī míng hù shi le yǐ qián zài yào diàn gōng zuò
why: 现在 + 是 + noun + 了 marks a new status, and 了 is natural with 是. This is correct.
en: She is a nurse now; she used to work in a pharmacy.
